name: Gona core-and-flake stone technology
description: At East Gona, hominins flaked stone cores, drawing on suitable cobbles likely collected from local gravels. Joins among East Gona 10 flakes preserve sequences from individual cobbles. The makers' identity remains unknown.

impact.note: Early production of sharp-edged flakes is documented at East Gona. Later Oldowan sites show both similar and distinct local patterns.

date.label: 2.6–2.5 million years ago
date.basis: Source reports geological age 2.6–2.5 Ma; calendar endpoints are rounded approximations and do not imply year-level precision.

events.statement: East Gona EG10 and EG12 stone artifacts are dated approximately 2.6–2.5 million years ago.

evidence.supports: Stone artifacts from the Gona sequence date approximately 2.6–2.5 million years ago.
The chapter dates EG10 and EG12 to 2.6–2.5 Ma, and describes sharp flakes, cores and fine-grained raw material selection.

evidence.locator: Introduction and site stratigraphy; Conjoining and refitting lithic sets from EG 10
evidence.supports: Identifies a probable local source of cobbles and reports physically refitted sets of flakes from East Gona 10.

contributions.group: Unidentified hominin toolmakers at East Gona

evidence.supports: Describes hominin manufacture of East Gona cores and flakes; species identity remains unknown.

events.scope: The dated event covers EG10 and EG12. The physical joins mentioned in the description were studied at EG10.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest date established for this specific documented case by the sources inspected; it does not establish an invention date or world priority.

caveats: The geological bounds are approximate, not exact calendar dates; the 1997 claim to global priority is outdated. Context dates do not identify a species or an invention date.

research.note: Independent check of date and archaeological scope against Semaw chapter 2; 1997 source remains abstract-only. Review of other facets remains open. The 2018 analysis adds EG10 observations from refitted pieces of the same archaeological assemblage.
